confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors come from three web searches. Uyuni-specific crowd-sourced data from Nomad Watch puts an inexpensive meal at about $2.9-3.6, beer at about $2.6-2.9 and coffee at about $2.0-2.2. National Bolivia figures are similar or slightly lower, and travel guides list tourist-restaurant mains at about $7-15. The sources disagree, and some older figures may assume an earlier boliviano exchange rate, so treat the USD values as uncertain. The mid-range meal for two is a bounded estimate based on mains of about $8-15 per person plus a starter or dessert. No direct cocktail or glass-of-wine prices were found for Uyuni. Those two anchors are scaled from the beer price and the Bolivian national price pattern, where Bolivian wine by the glass is modest and cocktails like the chuflay cost about 2-3x a beer in tourist bars. Accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge, not checked against live listings. Uyuni has many basic hostels, and its salt and three-star hotels charge above the Bolivian average. July is peak dry-season demand.
comparable_city_reasoning: Uyuni-specific crowd-sourced data where available, adjusted against Bolivian national averages and similar remote high-altitude tourist towns in the Andes (e.g., Tupiza, San Pedro de Atacama at a discount, Copacabana). Uyuni is cheap globally but priced slightly above other Bolivian towns because of its remote, tour-focused economy.
